# Ordinary data fanout — Go oracle producer

> The absolute paths below are the recorded batch 22e run on the measuring host. Substitute your own
> checkout for `/Users/zoujiaqing/projects/livekit-rs` and any writable directory for the
> `/private/tmp/...` staging paths; every driver takes them as flags.

**NEWLY AUTHORED** producer (`main.go`). The committed corpus (`fanout.jsonl`) is
**GENERATED by real execution of the pinned upstream Go server + protocol
module**, not hand-authored.

Consumer: `crates/rtc-media/src/regression.rs` →
`regression::actual_go_fanout_worker_count_and_synchronous_completion`,
bound to `ORDINARY_FANOUT_RESULTS`.

## Machine-bound artifact

`runtime_cpus` is Go's `runtime.NumCPU()` on the producing host — on macOS the
`CTL_HW`/`HW_NCPU` sysctl, **not** `GOMAXPROCS`. It must equal
`crate::data_fanout_cpu::count()` on the machine running the Rust test. This
corpus was produced and measured on **darwin/arm64 with `hw.ncpu = 10`**
(`sysctl -n hw.ncpu` → 10). On a host with a different logical CPU count the
`2*NumCPU` row and its `maximum_active` must be regenerated; the Rust test will
otherwise fail at the `runtime_cpus` assertion. `gomaxprocs` is emitted as an
extra transparency key only (it happened to also be 10 here).

## Coordinator run commands

```sh
GO="$HOME/go/pkg/mod/golang.org/toolchain@v0.0.1-go1.26.3.darwin-arm64/bin/go"
ROOT=/Users/zoujiaqing/projects/livekit-rs
STAGE=/private/tmp/b22e-rtc-stage

# 1. Stage (fresh dir required; verifies every manifest sha256; never runs Go).
python3 "$ROOT/tests/oracles/ordinary-fanout/prepare.py" \
  --root "$ROOT" --out "$STAGE/fanout-src"

# 2. Produce the corpus with real Go.
cd "$STAGE/fanout-src"
GOTOOLCHAIN=local GOPROXY=off GOWORK=off \
ORDINARY_FANOUT_RESULTS="$STAGE/fanout.jsonl" \
  "$GO" run .

# 3. Measure the Rust consumer against that real output (prebuilt binary, no cargo).
ORDINARY_FANOUT_RESULTS="$STAGE/fanout.jsonl" \
  "$ROOT/target/debug/deps/rtc_media-8255c958dfdb0d70" \
  --ignored --exact regression::actual_go_fanout_worker_count_and_synchronous_completion \
  --nocapture --test-threads=1
```

The output file is opened `O_CREATE|O_EXCL`, so a re-run needs a fresh path.

(`participants`, `runtime_cpus`, `returned_while_blocked`, `maximum_active`,

because it records real goroutine scheduling order.

## Why an external module instead of a `pkg/rtc` test stage

`rtc.BroadcastDataPacketForRoom` (`pkg/rtc/room.go:2119`) is **exported** and
takes the `types.Room` interface, and it is the exact function
`Room.SendDataPacket` (`room.go:843`) → `Room.onDataMessage` (`room.go:1292`)
reaches for the fanout. The pinned upstream `typesfakes.FakeRoom` and
`typesfakes.FakeLocalParticipant` therefore supply the room inventory and the
recipients without any in-package access. That avoids staging the whole server
tree, compiling the `pkg/rtc` test binary, and its Docker `TestMain`, while still
running the real fanout body. This is the `owner-metadata-errors` staging style:
copy the pinned `go.mod`, rename the module to `local.test/ordinary-fanout`, add
`require github.com/livekit/livekit-server v0.0.0` plus absolute replaces for
livekit-server, protocol, mediatransportutil and psrpc, and write `go.sum` as the
sorted, deduplicated **union of all four modules' `go.sum` lines**. `references/`
is never written to. `prometheus.Init("test", livekit.NodeType_SERVER)` and
`config.InitLoggerFromConfig` mirror the pinned `pkg/rtc/room_test.go` inits.

## What actually runs, and what is measured

Unchanged upstream code exercised by every row:

- the destination loop and the **single** `dpData, err = proto.Marshal(dp)`
  (`room.go:2166-2172`) whose buffer is shared by all recipients;
- `utils.ParallelExec(destParticipants, dataForwardLoadBalanceThreshold, 1, ...)`
  (`room.go:2177`) with the real unexported `dataForwardLoadBalanceThreshold = 4`
  (`room.go:58`);
- `protocol-stable/utils/parallel.go:54` — the `len(vals) < parallelThreshold`
  serial path (`:55`) and the `numCPU := runtime.NumCPU()` clamp to `len(vals)`
  (`:63`), the `atomic.Uint64` work-stealing index and `wg.Wait()`;
- the real argument tuple
  `op.SendDataMessage(kind, dpData, livekit.ParticipantID(dp.GetParticipantSid()), dp.GetSequence())`.

`wire_hex` is lowercase hex of those real `proto.Marshal` bytes (37 bytes for the
`UserPacket` payload `ordinary-fanout-actual-go-payload`). The producer asserts
all n recipients received **byte-identical** buffers (`distinct_wire_hex == 1`)
and that each buffer `proto.Unmarshal`s back to a `proto.Equal` copy of the sent
`DataPacket` (`round_trip_proto_equal`). `kind` is 0 (`RELIABLE`), `sender` is `""`
and `sequence` is 0 because the packet leaves `ParticipantSid`/`Sequence` unset.

**`maximum_active` is measured, not computed.** Every recipient stub records its
arguments, increments a shared `active` counter under a mutex, updates `peak`,
and then parks on a `release` channel. The producer polls `peak` until it has not
grown for 150 consecutive 1 ms samples, so all spawned workers are provably
parked inside the stub and `peak` is the number of workers `ParallelExec` really
created. It then samples whether the `BroadcastDataPacketForRoom` goroutine has
already finished (`returned_while_blocked`), closes `release`, and waits for
completion. Post-conditions checked with `panic`: `active == 0`, exactly n
distinct recipient calls, `sum(SendDataMessageCallCount()) == n`, one distinct
wire buffer, and `returned_while_blocked == false`. No expected worker count is
hardcoded anywhere in the producer.

Row selection `n = 3, 4, 2*NumCPU` covers below threshold (serial), at threshold
(parallel, `min(cpu, n) = n`), and CPU-clamped (`min(cpu, n) = cpu`).

## Scope

Admission-scheduling **component** proof, matching the Rust ignore reason
("admission scheduling component, not wire proof"). **Not** proven:

- Real `ParticipantImpl.SendDataMessage` behaviour downstream of the fanout — the
  recipients are pinned upstream `typesfakes.FakeLocalParticipant`, so the JOINING
  queue, the reliable/lossy writer selection and per-participant sequencing are
  not exercised here (the sibling `joining-reliable-queue` oracle covers the
  JOINING queue separately).
- Real ICE/DTLS/SCTP datachannel delivery, encryption, `BufferedAmount`
  back-pressure, slow-reader drops, or any physical wire transmission.
- `Room.onDataMessage` upstream of `BroadcastDataPacketForRoom`: duplicate-nonce
  dropping is exercised only as `FakeRoom.IsDataMessageUserPacketDuplicateReturns(false)`,
  and `DestinationIdentities`/`DestinationSids` filtering is exercised only in the
  empty (broadcast-to-all) case. Source-self exclusion is not exercised
  (`source == nil`).
- Real room membership, participant readiness, or `Room` locking; the inventory
  is `FakeRoom.GetLocalParticipantsReturns`.
- Any claim about a host other than the one that produced the artifact: worker
  counts are a function of that host's `runtime.NumCPU()`.
- Timing/latency: `peak_stable_millis` is the producer's own stabilization
  window, not an upstream measurement, and `arrival_order` is
  scheduling-dependent extra evidence rather than a stable contract.

No Rust source, no existing oracle and no reference input was modified.
